question: How did possession of coastal nodes become more than military occupation?
mechanism: Ports and forts lowered coercion/logistics costs; declining profitability and territorial obligations increased incentives for taxation, land revenue, registration and legal control.
transmission_channel: Fortified coastal nodes and VOC administrative institutions linked military control to fiscal registration, land administration and legal categorisation.
time_lag: Multi-decade transition from coastal conquest/consolidation to deeper eighteenth-century fiscal-administrative legibility.
scale: Z1 coastal nodes → Z2 colonial territorial administration.
confounders: regional variation in VOC administrative penetration
transportability: Mechanism-only. Fort possession can enable administrative penetration, but the degree and social effects depend on local institutions and cannot be transported as a universal colonial sequence.
integration_action: Use in A06 to connect fort/logistics control to registration and fiscal legibility; retain local variation and avoid claiming that forts alone caused bureaucratic transformation.
